item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong direct evidence for professionalized funding/management of children’s policy, disaster relief, healthcare/nursing-care subsidies, local grants, and budget setting through formal councils and expert input. I found little direct evidence of patronage within social-service agencies themselves. The main negative evidence is indirect: scandal pressure, coalition bargaining, and fragile macro conditions. I did not find a clear 2024 example of Kishida openly using social-service budgets to reward loyalists or bypass competent administrators.","evidence":[{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-30","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"Kishida tied 2024 to wage growth, child support, disaster recovery, women’s participation, public education, dementia policy, and regional revitalization, and said funding would come through expenditure reform. That is strong evidence of formal, programmatic social-service management rather than patronage.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.2","6B.3","5B.6","5B.8"]},{"title":"Policies supporting children and child-rearing","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024 page content","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/childsupport.html","summary":"The cabinet page lays out a structured package: child allowances, reduced childbirth and higher-education burdens, housing support for child-rearing households, prenatal/postnatal care, and stronger early-childhood education and childcare. This is policy design through administrative systems, not clientelist handouts.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.2","6B.3"]},{"title":"Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-04-19","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202404/19keizai.html","summary":"Kishida said regional revitalization required sustainable local services, digital tools, and grants, indicating social-service administration that tries to build capacity in poorer areas through ordinary public institutions.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.3","6B.2"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-06-21","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida backed expanded subsidies for school lunches, agriculture, SMEs, medical and nursing care, childcare, school facilities, public transport, logistics, regional tourism, and low-income households. The package was routed through formal policy channels and aimed at broad service delivery, not partisan distribution.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.2","6B.3","5B.8"]},{"title":"Meeting of Experts to Review Active Cyber Defense","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-06-07","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html","summary":"Although not a welfare policy, it shows the broader governing style: Kishida convened a 17-expert panel to shape legislation, which is consistent with a technocratic approach to state capacity rather than patronage networks.","question_ids":["6B.4","5B.2","5B.6"]},{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-30","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"The same speech also says the government would pursue reskilling, labor-market reform, infrastructure, capital investment, and cyber/legal preparation through formal policy structures. That supports a reading of professionalized public management rather than personal-network control.","question_ids":["6B.4","5B.6","5B.7"]},{"title":"Prime Minister Kishida’s Statements after the Earthquake Response","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-25","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html","summary":"The disaster package used cash aid, emergency housing, reduced medical/nursing-care burdens, and support for schools and transit, which is targeted service delivery through the state rather than patronage.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.2","6B.3","5B.9"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-03-19","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/19kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida accepted the BOJ’s judgment that a price-wage virtuous cycle had been confirmed and said the government would preserve the existing accord, which is evidence of rule-based macro management supporting public-service funding stability.","question_ids":["6B.4","5B.3","5B.7","5B.10"]},{"title":"July 29 budget-guidelines decision","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-07-29","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html","summary":"Kishida approved budget guidelines based on medium- to long-term projections and framed policy around private-demand-led growth and wage increases above inflation. That is technocratic budget management, not patronage budgeting.","question_ids":["6B.4","5B.1","5B.7","5B.10"]},{"title":"Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-02-28","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362","summary":"Reuters reported Kishida was pulled into defensive political management over the funding scandal, which suggests some budget and reform decisions were shaped by short-term survival pressure rather than purely professional administration.","question_ids":["6B.4","5B.5","5B.7","5B.10"]},{"title":"Japan’s Kishida championed new capitalism but was undone by yen","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen","summary":"Reuters says Kishida achieved major wage gains, but the weak yen and high prices blunted results; that is mixed evidence that competent management did not fully overcome external constraints.","question_ids":["6B.4","5B.7","5B.10","6B.2"]},{"title":"Kishida will not run for reelection","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455","summary":"Reuters framed his exit as driven by scandals and living-cost anger, which shows political pressure was shaping the governing environment even where the policy apparatus was professional.","question_ids":["6B.4","5B.5","5B.7","6B.2"]}]}
